title: Cross-screen analysis of insulin-content effects among cytokine-survival-favoring beta-cell knockouts
author: UCP Technology LLC

pages.text: Cross-screen analysis of insulin-content effects among cytokine-survival-favoring beta-cell knockouts

UCP Technology LLC
Revised research report | 24 October 2026
Abstract

Whether beta-cell vulnerability can be reduced while preserving insulin production and glucose-responsive release motivates this comparison. We compared published cytokine-survival and intracellular insulin-content knockout catalogs in EndoC-betaH1 cells using explicit coverage and expression-based eligibility rules. Among 12,184 eligible genes, 14 of 285 survival-favoring targets (4.91%) had published lower-content calls, versus 465 of 11,899 other genes (3.91%). The conditional odds ratio was 1.2347 (exact 95% CI 0.6597-2.1336), with one-sided enrichment p=0.2634; enrichment remains unresolved. Across all 427 source survival-favoring genes, 15 have published lower-content and 2 higher-content evidence; 285 meet primary eligibility. NUPL1 retains lower-content evidence despite missing the exact expression-symbol match. Post-review inspection identified precision loss in deposited guide probabilities; the unsupported independent guide-significance claim is withdrawn, without changing primary catalog membership or estimates. The resource identifies perturbations for testing whether apparent rescue preserves function, temporarily suppresses it, or reflects altered secretion, growth or selection. These separate screens do not establish a causal survival-function trade-off.
Protecting beta cells while preserving function

Is the biology that supports insulin production and release also part of what makes a beta cell vulnerable, and can those properties be separated? The objective is durable, glucose-responsive insulin output from a surviving population through injury and recovery. Secretory load, functional state and stress resistance are already connected questions in beta-cell research [3,6,11]. The present study supplies specific perturbations and an explicit comparison framework with which to investigate that relationship; it does not claim to discover the broader question.

Benaglio et al. measured relative knockout representation after cytokine exposure; Rottner et al. measured representation in low versus high intracellular insulin bins [1,2]. We quantify their overlap against a common measurable background and retain evidence separately from eligibility. A survival-favoring/lower-content candidate motivates a causal question, not a diagnosis of functional loss. Reduced stores could reflect biosynthesis, release, degradation or cell state; relative enrichment could reflect death, proliferation or selection. The unresolved aggregate association establishes neither a universal trade-off nor independence.

pages.text: Positive survival beta denotes knockout enrichment under cytokines relative to untreated culture; positive insulin low/high log2 fold change (LFC) denotes enrichment in the low-insulin bin. These are different effect scales. The separate treatment-duration cell-count experiment reported with n=3 in Benaglio is not evidence for three independent genome-wide survival screens. Source-specific replication and sampling details are retained in the design record.
Guide probability precision limits the original audit

All 142,180 S8 FDR values are stored as zero (99,564) or one (42,616), not merely displayed that way. All 2,384 uniquely linked S7 rows have S8 FDR values equal to nearest-integer rounding of the continuous S7 value. For a matched TOMM6 guide, S7 FDR 0.42555 becomes S8 zero. The linked rows demonstrate lost FDR precision. The workbook's saved Power Query import explicitly assigns Int64.Type to all four S8 probability columns while retaining numeric LFC/counts. The original reanalysis interpreted stored FDR <0.10 as guide significance; this interpretation is withdrawn. Full-precision genome-wide original output was not recovered.

The deposited author code also uses count thresholds, replication of the same guide coordinate, an expression lookup and an explicit gene exclusion [5]. Our former per-replicate rule was not a reconstruction of that pipeline. Among primary genes absent from Table S1, 2,421 nevertheless satisfy the former positive-LFC/stored-zero rule in at least two guides per replicate. S7 preserves continuous FDRs for a selected subset; we use those values only for explicitly available candidate guides, without treating absent S7 guides as nonsignificant.
Eligibility and evidence are different axes

pages.caption: Figure 1. Candidate flow through common coverage and the expression restriction. Published screen evidence remains recorded when a candidate is excluded from the primary analysis.
pages.alt: Flow from 427 survival-favoring genes to 390 with common coverage, with 37 coverage losses, and then 285 primary-eligible genes, with 105 additional expression-related exclusions. NUPL1 retains its published lower-content call outside the primary set.

pages.text: Exact symbols are joined after trimming whitespace, with no silent alias repair. Survival eligibility requires a unique finite record, at least three guides and no hsa- prefix. Insulin coverage requires at least three guide identities with valid paired rows and normalized count sum at least 20 in each replicate; control targets are excluded. This is a declared cross-screen measurability rule, not the source publication's hit-selection rule.

The primary expression restriction requires a unique finite Table S5 GeneName-to-baseMean match and baseMean at least 10. All duplicated expression names are excluded. This proxy comes from CALCOCO2-silencing/control RNA-seq; it selects a population with measured expression in that experiment and does not fully adjust for biological detectability or reconstruct the original screen filter. Removing or changing it is a sensitivity analysis.

NUPL1 illustrates the distinction: survival beta 0.40897, survival FDR 0.05641, a published Decrease call and 4 covered guides are available. Its primary exclusion is no exact expression symbol. The evidence field preserves the lower-content call independently of this adjustment-variable exclusion.
Conditional catalog association

Within the primary universe, exposure A denotes positive survival beta with the original survival FDR <0.10; outcome L denotes a published insulin Decrease label. Strata cross quintiles of log2(baseMean+1), survival-guide coverage 3-5 versus 6+, and insulin-guide coverage 3 versus 4+. With stratum size n, exposed count m and outcome count k, the fixed-margin likelihood is:
Fixed-margin noncentral hypergeometric likelihood

We maximize the product likelihood and convolve stratum distributions. Inclusive tail inversion gives an equal-tailed 95% interval; the one-sided enrichment p-value is the upper tail at odds ratio 1. The original success criterion is a lower interval bound above 1. Exactness is conditional on the independent-stratum, common-odds fixed-margin working model. Gene dependence, odds-ratio heterogeneity and source-screen selection uncertainty are not modeled.
Published-catalog enrichment remains unresolved

The published-only primary comparison has 14/285 lower-content calls among survival-favoring genes versus 465/11,899 among the remaining eligible genes. The conditional odds ratio is 1.2347 (exact 95% CI 0.6597-2.1336); one-sided enrichment p=0.2634. Removing the invalid stored-FDR audit leaves the original primary membership, strata and numerical estimate unchanged. The unstratified conditional estimate is 1.2703 (0.6798-2.1907).

pages.caption: Figure 2. Full-range gene-level effect displays for both insulin replicates. All primary genes form the background; survival-favoring genes are colored by their published content call. Median guide LFC summarizes direction and magnitude, without treating binary deposited FDR values as valid significance estimates.
pages.alt: Two full-range scatterplots show survival beta against median insulin guide LFC for all primary genes, highlighting survival-favoring candidates with published lower-content, higher-content or no directional calls. Outliers remain visible.

pages.text: Of 427 source survival-favoring genes, 390 have common coverage and 285 enter the primary comparison. Across the full resource, 15 have published lower-content evidence, 2 higher-content evidence, 384 have an insulin measurement without a published directional call, and 26 lack an exact insulin-screen gene measurement. Only 14 of the 15 lower-content candidates are primary-eligible.

Neither a confidence interval crossing 1 nor repeated inconclusive sensitivity analyses demonstrate equivalence. The estimate remains compatible with lower odds or a materially larger overlap under the declared working model.

pages.text: Biology that changes interpretation

A bounded annotation review separates direct beta-cell perturbation evidence from general cellular-process annotation. The complete 15-candidate annotation includes NUPL1 and records sources, model context, plausible alternatives and untested endpoints. The examples below show why lower content and impaired function are not interchangeable, and why stress context matters.

pages.caption: Table 4. Independent evidence that informs follow-up, with model-specific limits.
rows: SSR2 depletion/knockout in rat INS832/13 cells reduced proinsulin biosynthesis and insulin storage, with rescue evidence; the glucose-stimulated fold response remained robust. [6]
Lower content is not synonymous with loss of glucose sensing; an unchanged fold response is not proof of preserved total secretory capacity.
NCOA6 depletion impaired glucose-responsive insulin secretion in EndoC-betaH1; beta-cell conditional mouse deletion also impaired secretion and MAFA-target expression. [7]
The human cell-line secretion experiment was content-normalized; mouse deletion began developmentally. Neither is a matched cytokine protection experiment.
Cnop et al. found that CREB3 silencing increased palmitate-induced apoptosis in INS-1E cells, primary rat beta cells and two human islet preparations. [8]
Palmitate and cytokines are different insults; this independent evidence warns against a universal survival-favoring interpretation.
Genetic NCLX suppression altered mitochondrial/cytosolic calcium signals in MIN6 and primary beta-cell experiments and delayed glucose-dependent insulin secretion. [9]
The observed temporal secretion phenotype in rodent systems is not simultaneous human inflammatory survival/function validation.

pages.text: Cellular-process membership supports a mechanistic question, not a validated mechanism for this cross-screen association. A published phenotype in a rodent beta-cell model does not demonstrate the same effect in EndoC-betaH1 cells or under the cytokine selection conditions. No candidate in this resource has acquired matched-condition validation merely by appearing in both catalogs.
Distinct candidates test distinct explanations

SSR2 motivates a biosynthetic-demand hypothesis [6]; NCOA6 motivates transcriptional competence and functional identity [7]; SLC8B1 motivates secretion timing [9]. UBE2C's association with compensatory beta-cell proliferation in a mouse knockout study makes growth versus death a necessary distinction [10]. These candidates need not share a mechanism. Their annotations select informative measurements; none establishes that a functional downshift causes protection in the cytokine screen.
Separating protection from functional suppression

These four explanations are hypotheses for matched experiments and can coexist: a protective downshift might also be reversible. The next study asks which perturbations protect without lasting loss of glucose-responsive function and whether any functional suppression contributes to protection or accompanies it.

pages.caption: Table 5. Competing explanations and discriminating predictions.
rows: Independently reversing the downshift while retaining the original perturbation attenuates protection, with direct effects addressed. Necessity would require preventing the downshift to remove the protective effect under the tested conditions.
Functional restoration can coexist with protection when the original perturbation is retained and the functional branch is manipulated independently.
Activity falls during injury but surviving cells recover glucose-responsive output after the insult and, where applicable, suppression are withdrawn.
The apparent trade-off reflects endpoints or selection
Relative enrichment occurs without less absolute death, or reduced stores coexist with maintained glucose-responsive release. Growth and population selection explain part of the signal.

pages.text: Intervene on the proposed mediator

First establish absolute survival and function in the same model, perturbation and condition. Then vary the proposed mediator independently while holding the original perturbation in place, with mediator-only controls and measurement of direct effects on injury. Original-gene rescue supports an on-target effect; reversing both phenotypes does not establish mediation. Verify that the mediator actually changed: content alone does not measure biosynthetic load. Suppression alone producing protection tests sufficiency, not necessity. Protection retained with the specified functional deficit prevented or restored supports separability in that setting; unsuccessful rescue attempts do not establish an unavoidable trade-off.
Measure function through injury and recovery

Follow matched populations before, during and after injury; distinguish cytokine withdrawal from withdrawal of the perturbation. A permanent knockout followed by cytokine removal cannot test withdrawal of protective suppression. Compare transient and sustained interventions only after demonstrating that the intervention and relevant cellular program are reversible. Track surviving cells to distinguish recovery from replacement or selection. Measure death, proliferation, insulin production and storage, basal and glucose-responsive release, timing, and both total output and output per viable beta cell. Predefine durability and justified equivalence or noninferiority margins for the specified functions; nonsignificance is insufficient. Cumulative insulin output alone cannot establish preservation when basal release, responsiveness or timing is abnormal.
Candidate tests and interpretation decisions

Table 6 translates the framework into illustrative decisions after matched phenotypes are established. The proposed interventions require validation in the chosen model; the cited studies motivate the variables, not proven mediator-specific tools. Independent intervention controls must separate mediator effects from direct injury or broad fitness changes.

pages.caption: Table 6. Candidate-specific causal and selection tests proposed for follow-up.
headers: Independent variable with the original perturbation retained
rows: Independently titrate proinsulin expression. Verify nascent synthesis and ER entry; changing transcript abundance alone may not restore the relevant load.
If measured load can be restored and protection attenuates, load suppression may contribute. Failure to alter ER throughput is an unsuccessful mediator test, not evidence against mediation.
NCOA6: a defined secretory transcriptional program [7]
Independently restore a validated downstream module, such as selected MAFA-target expression, while NCOA6 remains suppressed. Require functional rescue beyond marker expression.

Protection retained within a prespecified margin while the secretion deficit is reversed supports separability. Loss of protection may support contribution only after direct effects of module restoration are addressed.
UBE2C: proliferative expansion rather than reduced death [10]
Independently vary cell-cycle progression and track divisions and deaths, with matched intervention-only controls.

If extra representation disappears with proliferation control while death is unchanged, this supports a growth contribution to the enrichment. Reduced death supports a survival component that still requires functional assessment.

pages.text: Include contrasting content phenotypes

pages.caption: Table 7. Higher-content comparison candidates from the same resource.

pages.text: RAB14 and LRRC61 broaden the proposed panel beyond lower-content candidates. Higher stores could reflect altered release or storage and do not establish improved glucose-responsive secretion or safer physiology. Apply the same absolute survival, basal release, stimulated output and recovery criteria. A survival-favoring candidate with no published content call remains functionally unresolved.
Sensitivity questions and information limits

pages.caption: Figure 4. Published-catalog estimates grouped by the question changed: expression universe, exposure threshold or survival comparator. These overlapping analyses reuse the source data and are not independent confirmations. The positive-versus-negative comparison directly addresses survival-direction specificity.
pages.alt: Forest plot with exact 95% intervals for the primary catalog and six related analyses. All intervals cross odds ratio 1, including the direct survival-favoring versus survival-harming comparison.

pages.text: The direct survival-favoring versus survival-harming estimate is 1.1871 (exact 95% CI 0.4830-2.9863); it does not establish direction-specific enrichment. Without the expression restriction, the published catalog includes TOMM6 and yields 17,276 genes, 390 exposed targets and 15 overlaps, with OR 1.3155 (exact 95% CI 0.7233-2.2194). All 7 revised catalog intervals include 1.

Only 14 exposed outcome-positive genes and 12 informative strata among 20 retained strata support the primary association. Holding observed margins fixed, the null expected overlap is 11.52; the original lower-95%-bound criterion first succeeds at 19 overlaps. Its conditional probability is 31.3% if the common OR is 1.5 and 75.7% if it is 2.0. These fixed-margin illustrations are not prospective wet-lab power calculations and do not propagate original-screen uncertainty. A large gene denominator does not supply many independent exposed outcome-positive observations.

A separate one-to-one HGNC/Ensembl mapping sensitivity includes 12,826 genes and 306 exposed targets, with 14 overlaps: OR 1.1444 (exact 95% CI 0.6124-1.9735), p=0.3537. NUPL1 enters as NUP58, while the SLC24A6/SLC8B1 many-to-one collision is excluded rather than merged. Every mapping and exclusion is recorded; this post-review sensitivity does not alter the exact-symbol primary.

The two original three-guide calculations are retained as historical stored-zero-rule diagnostics in the release. They do not establish stronger statistical evidence. Revised model outputs, historical numerical outputs and the source-semantic findings are explicitly separated.
Scope, adjacent work and scientific use

Okino et al. combine an EndoC-betaH1 thapsigargin survival screen with stress co-expression analysis and prior insulin-content regulators [3]. Van Tienhoven et al. reported stress-associated accelerated insulin mRNA decay with improved human-islet vitality and function [11]; this supports considering adaptive load regulation, without establishing recovery after withdrawal or the mechanism of any candidate here. Our cytokine-screen comparison adds a common measurable denominator, quantified uncertainty and exhaustive evidence/eligibility accounting. It makes no claim of a first survival-function connection or a causal trade-off. Howe et al. address the further question of transport from cellular phenotypes to human diabetes evidence [4].

Gene dependence, source-hit uncertainty, off-target effects, unequal assay conditions and the expression proxy lie outside the fixed-margin sampling model. Repeated numerical agreement shares these source limitations; the guide-probability correction shows why computation alone cannot validate measurement meaning.

The resource provides perturbations with which to ask whether apparent rescue preserves beta-cell function, temporarily suspends it, or selects a population with persistently low output. Independent mediator intervention and recovery measurements are needed to identify where protection and functional loss can be separated. Neither the candidate overlap nor the unresolved aggregate association answers that question. A no-call or an eligibility exclusion is never evidence that function is preserved.

We measured cross-screen associations between relative cytokine-survival enrichment and intracellular insulin-content effects in a human beta-cell line; we did not measure prevention, remission, insulin independence, functional cure or biological cure.
Versioning and reproducibility

The original protocol, arithmetic and unique earlier research are retained as historical material. Version 2 amends guide-probability interpretation and evidence/eligibility accounting after review; additional numerical diagnostics are exploratory. The causal and recovery framework is proposed, not performed. Inputs are deposited processed records, not reconstructed sequencing reads. The release supplies pinned inputs, original and revised calculations, generated tables, and code/data licensing notices. AI-assisted development and computational reconstruction do not substitute for biological validation.

Each build generates headline facts and tables from scientific results and checks dependency hashes and input consistency. The release includes reproducibility instructions, a native Word equation and descriptive figure alternative text.

Supplement: continuous effects and influence

We compare mean per-gene median LFC within each stratum and weight differences by the observed share of exposed genes, m_s/285. This targets the exposure-group stratum composition rather than weighting strata equally. For r0, the contrast is -0.0393 log2 units (95% gene-bootstrap percentile interval -0.1073 to 0.0310). For r1, the contrast is 0.0341 log2 units (95% gene-bootstrap percentile interval -0.1038 to 0.1632).

pages.text: Omitting each informative stratum in turn gives conditional OR estimates from 0.9485 to 1.4958; all 12 intervals include 1. This is an influence diagnostic with changing fixed margins, not a set of independent replication tests.

The bootstrap resamples genes jointly across the two insulin replicates within each exposure-by-stratum group. Singleton groups contribute no empirical within-group bootstrap variability, and pathway dependence can make these intervals optimistic. Full per-stratum sample sizes, weights, effect summaries and leave-one-stratum-out estimates are supplied. These diagnostics explain the original result; they do not replace its endpoint or success criterion.
